title: Warn on unrecognized Content-Transfer-Encoding values
description:
map_encoding() in parse.rs silently maps any unrecognized CTE token to TransferEncoding::Identity with no indication anything unusual happened. The caller gets raw bytes with no flag.

Fix: when the wildcard arm fires (Encoding::None and the CTE string is not 7bit/8bit/binary/x-uuencode/x-uue/uuencode), push a warning to the warnings Vec if the CTE value is non-empty.

NOTE: x-uuencode/x-uue/uuencode are handled by MIME-80l.3 and must NOT trigger the warning.

Acceptance criteria:
- CTE: x-gzip produces a warning containing the unrecognized value
- CTE: x-bzip2 produces a warning
- Absent CTE (no header at all) produces no warning
- CTE: 7bit / 8bit / binary / quoted-printable / base64 produce no warning
- CTE: x-uuencode / x-uue / uuencode produce no warning (handled separately)
- TransferEncoding::Identity is still returned in all unrecognized cases
- Add tests for all cases above

Blocked by MIME-80l.3 (must know which values are recognized before wiring the warning).
